main_text.p: um, & intoentium animos ad libidinem so-licitat citius, quàm ad honestam opinionem. Decet autem vt virgo tota & vndique virgo sit, nec vlla ex parte det corruptæ mentis fi-gnificationem.

Quarto loquitur de impatietia correptionis spiritus in carnalibus hominibus prisci seculi. Ait enim, Non contendet spiritus meus cum homine in perpetuum: vel, vt Lutherus vertit: Die menschen wöllen sich meinen geist nicht mehr straffen lassen: eò quòd ipsi caro sunt, id est, quia carnalibus operibus seipsos totos dedunt, & animæ substantia abutuntur, & quasi sola carne circundati anima carerent, sic vitam suam abfumunt: quemadmodum Chrysost. ait.

Alij autem hæc Dei verba sic exponunt: Spiritus meus. i. verbi mei arguens per ministros prophetas mundum de peccato, non amplius homines iudicabit aut corripiet. Est vero hæc grauissima pœna, subtractio vi del. verbi Dei, Amos. 8. Sunt prætere a qui interpretantur spiritum Dei, de vitali spiritu, quem homini Deus sit adempturus, adducto in terram diluvio: qui spiritus, Dei spiritus appelletur, vt a Deo Adamo inspiratus.

Postremò fit hoc loco mentio annorum 120. ad pœnitentiam assignatorum, quibus resipiscerent: qui locus de lenitate Dei est, pœ-ni ad ignoscendum, de qua Luc.12. Rom. 2.1. Pet.3.& 2.Pet. 3. Diluvium enim subito non invehit,

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "intoentium" as printed; "fi-gnificationem" hyphen partly visible; "videl." at the line end "vi" has no clear hyphen, so it may be "vi-del." or a damaged word; "assignatorum" is printed "a fignatorum" with a space, probably a printer's split; "resipiscerent" is printed with blurred letters; "pœ-ni" reads as a broken word, possibly "pœnitentiam" in part; the Fraktur "meinen geist" in the German line is partly blurred, the second word may read "gĕist". Printed "120." is read as arabic numerals. Long s is normalised to s throughout, including "Chrysost." and "sit".
